findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison endpoint contrasts are strongest and most reproducible for short-range pair kernels: pair_kernel_1.5 (integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (-0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive fraction 0.0). Raw and adjusted branch correlations agree in sign for the 1.5 and 2.5 shells (e.g. branch_adjusted:163, :164, :240, :241). These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a radial pair-distance shell density, not absolute geometric descriptors or interaction energies.

Shape anisotropy carries signed endpoint contrast: shape_yy is negative and highly significant (integrated z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0) and shape_xx is negative (q 8.1e-4), while shape_xz is positive but not significant (q 0.219). The same sign pattern appears in the raw and adjusted branch correlations (branch_adjusted:158, :235) and in the per-landmark local_cyy enrichment z, which is negative at every landmark (regional_effects:5, :15, :75, :85, :105, :125, :135, :145, :155, :165, :175, :185, :195). Shape entries are coordinate covariance descriptors in A^2, not a chemical mechanism.

Landmark occupancy and soft-minimum contrasts are heterogeneous in sign across landmarks rather than a single global direction: occupancy3 is positive at landmark 00 (z 0.545, q 2.4e-4) and negative at landmarks 01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 12, 15, 18 (e.g. -0.376, -0.038, -0.007, -0.005, -0.009, -0.107, -0.017, -0.058), while softmin is negative at landmark 00 (-0.481) and positive at landmarks 01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 12, 15, 18 (e.g. 0.225, 0.253, 0.360, 0.396, 0.294, 0.335, 0.369, 0.264). The corresponding regional enrichment z rows show the same per-landmark sign split. Occupancy is a radial shell density and softmin a normalized soft-minimum distance; neither is monotone in distance or a quality axis.

Global centroid contrasts are weak and not reproducible: global_centroid_x (z -0.111, q 0.257), global_centroid_y (z -0.243, q 0.0136) and global_centroid_z (z -0.061, q 0.481) have low positive batch fractions (0.36, 0.21, 0.43), and the raw and adjusted branch covariance rows for the same features are near zero with p above 0.7. Centroid is a translation coordinate in A, so this is a weak pose-level signal, not a shape or interaction effect.

Descendant survival credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity. Its strongest positive rows are landmark_00_soft_mass (z 0.365, q 0.120), landmark_07_soft_mass (0.220, q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (0.234, q 0.302), landmark_18_local_czz (0.217, q 0.302) and landmark_04_local_cyz (rate z 1.79, q 0.302), while several local_cyy and local_czz rows are negative (e.g. landmark_05_local_czz -0.419, landmark_09_local_czz -0.390, landmark_16_local_cyy -0.317). Because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, none of these can be presented as final affinity benefit.

Parent-child increment contrasts disagree with the whole-window endpoint contrasts in several places. landmark_00_softmin has a negative increment rate (z -4.91, q 0.046) and landmark_00_occupancy3 a positive one (z 4.28, q 0.081), while shape_xx and shape_yy increments are negative (z -3.70 and -3.85, q 0.095 and 0.161) and shape_xz positive (z 3.00, q 0.207). This disagreement is evidence that within-path change and changing cohort composition are not interchangeable, and it should affect direction priorities rather than being averaged away.

Turnover accounting separates population rate, edge rate and residual. For landmark_00_soft_mass the population rate is small (z 0.185) while the edge rate is large (z 4.55) and the residual is negative (z -4.36); for landmark_00_local_cxx and landmark_00_local_cyy the residuals are strongly positive (z 4.29 and 5.05, q 0.038 and 0.033). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolations over the complete observed window [0.0, 0.49] with extrapolation disallowed, and they show many sign changes and strong first-to-last rate reversals. Examples: landmark_00_local_dx has first_rate_z -17.5 and last_rate_z 8.1 with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts; landmark_00_local_cxy has 9 sign changes and 14 strong sign conflicts; landmark_02_local_cyz has first_rate_z 57.3 and last_rate_z 5.7 with 9 sign changes. Polynomial fits are rejected (polynomial_accepted false) and relative node RMSE is often 0.6-1.0, so a constant rule is not supported over a time-conditioned rule, and no arbitrary time bins or extrapolation are warranted. A contrast curve is not an absolute reward target.

Joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment (0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and with teacher innovation-contrast alignment (0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0), but negatively associated with observed child score gain (-0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast is dominated by its internal fraction (0.787) with smaller translation (0.132) and rotation (0.081) fractions. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal effects.

Joint motion diagnostics are consistently negative and reproducible: joint_innovation_RMS_A (raw z -5.15e-5, q 0.038, positive batch fraction 0.857; adjusted z -3.60e-5, q 0.020, 0.929), joint_internal_RMS_A (raw q 0.044, adjusted q 0.030) and joint_translation_RMS_A (raw q 0.095, adjusted q 0.072). The raw and adjusted correlations for the same features agree in sign (e.g. branch_adjusted:228 and :305). These are joint-motion summaries, not atom velocities or causal selection effects.

Coverage and support limits are explicit: the information audit reports 14 independent batches and states that the geometric nearest-teacher comparison is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that nonnegative excess distance is by construction; curve_support selects 24 curves under a fidelity rule with relative RMSE up to 0.35 and zero strong sign conflicts, and reports quiet-node large-fit fractions up to 0.34; lineage_support reports 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, with BH correction over 400 survival tests. Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Teacher and control bindings are fixed: 28 static teachers with assignment RMS quantiles [0.446, 0.863, 1.050] A, temperature_edits false, and fixed parameters mixture_temperature 0.5 and teacher_endpoint_temperature_A2 4.0. The incumbent uses the FLOWR endpoint VJP with pointcloud_delta_A 1.0 A, teacher_neighbors 4, contrast bound 2.0 nats and no affinity-head gradient. The registered bounded edits are pointcloud_delta_A in {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} A, teacher_neighbors in {2, 4, 8}, temporal_teacher_blend in {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}, and evidence-bound region or temporal-region indices. Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Testable coordinate intervention: observable is the signed favorable-minus-comparison contrast on the short-range pair-kernel shells (1.5-3.5 A) at the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window; intended response is a positive shift in that contrast; target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward with the real FLOWR endpoint VJP and detached matching convention; spatial scale is the 1.5-3.5 A pair-distance shell; temporal scale is the full observed window [0.0, 0.49]. A discriminating failure condition is that the short-range shell contrast does not increase while the 7.0 A shell contrast does, or that the effect is not reproducible across the 14 independent batches. This could be expressed by the registered pointcloud_delta_A edit (0.5, 1.0 or 2.0 A) or by an evidence-bound region index, but the contrast itself is a measurable target, not an absolute reward target.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable is the signed contrast on shape_yy (and the co-signed shape_xx) together with the per-landmark local_cyy enrichment z; intended response is a negative shift in shape_yy contrast; target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward; spatial scale is the global shape tensor plus the 5 A landmark neighborhoods; temporal scale is the full observed window. A discriminating failure condition is that shape_yy contrast does not decrease while shape_xz contrast does, or that the per-landmark local_cyy signs do not stay negative. This remains descriptive unless a permitted reward recipe can express it, since the executing pointcloud scalar has no explicit shape-tensor term.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable is the per-landmark occupancy3/occupancy5 and softmin contrast pair; intended response is a landmark-specific sign pattern (positive occupancy3 with negative softmin at landmark 00, and the opposite at landmarks 01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 12, 15, 18); target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward with an evidence-bound region index; spatial scale is the 5 A landmark neighborhood with shell radii 3 and 5 A; temporal scale is the full observed window. A discriminating failure condition is that the landmark-specific sign pattern does not reproduce across the 14 independent batches, or that a single global occupancy direction fits better than the per-landmark split.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable is the time-conditioned signed contrast from the observed-node linear curves; intended response is a time-varying sign pattern rather than a constant rule; target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward with the temporal_teacher_blend recipe; spatial scale is the landmark or pair-kernel feature; temporal scale is the observed window [0.0, 0.49] with no extrapolation. A discriminating failure condition is that a constant rule matches the observed-node interpolation within its relative node RMSE, or that the sign changes are not reproducible across batches. The registered temporal_teacher_blend values (0.25, 0.5, 1.0) are the permitted expression; the contrast curve is not an absolute reward target.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable is the parent-child increment contrast together with the turnover residual; intended response is a within-path change that is not explained by changing cohort composition; target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward; spatial scale is the landmark or shape feature; temporal scale is the full observed window. A discriminating failure condition is that the increment contrast and the turnover residual move together with the population rate, which would indicate reclassification or parent weighting rather than within-path change. The residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable is the joint innovation and internal RMS contrast together with the teacher innovation-contrast alignment; intended response is a reduction in joint internal RMS contrast while teacher alignment stays positive; target origin is the endpoint pointcloud reward with the real FLOWR endpoint VJP; spatial scale is the joint pose and internal geometry; temporal scale is the full observed window. A discriminating failure condition is that joint internal RMS contrast does not decrease while observed child score gain does, or that the negative innovation-to-score-gain association is not reproducible across the 14 independent batches. These are joint-motion summaries, not atom velocities or causal selection effects.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters; no temperature edit is proposed.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so moment and kernel findings are diagnostic only.
